source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Sabey Ashburn Building A publishes 54 MW of IT capacity, the only figure on the record that bears on AI scaling.

The certifications, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001 and SSAE 18, qualify the campus to host workloads with financial reporting controls, payment card data, protected health information and general enterprise security requirements. They say nothing about which tenants are actually there, and the operator does not publish that. The address and postal code are listed, and no power source, utility, substation, cooling design, rack count or accelerator count is published at all.

To turn 54 MW into a sense of scale requires an assumption the operator does not make. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 54 MW of IT load is roughly 1,350 racks, since 54,000 kW divided by 40 kW per rack equals 1,350. At a lower 10 kW per rack, a density typical of older enterprise halls, the same load is about 5,400 racks. Neither figure is Sabey's claim, and the real number depends on cooling and power distribution the spec page does not describe. What the 54 MW does establish is a ceiling on the site's draw, not a statement about what is installed.

In Virginia this campus ranks tenth among the 29 facilities in the state that publish a megawatt figure, against a published state total of 2,563.4 MW. That places it at roughly 2 percent of the state's published capacity. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities, and most of them publish no figure at all, so the 29 with numbers are a small and self-selected slice of the state's actual footprint. The rank is real within the published set and says nothing about the unpublished rest.
